---
title: "Clean: minimum wage"
---

The minimum wage CSV from [scrape_minimum_wage.qmd](scrape_minimum_wage.qmd) has more columns than the chart needs. The code below keeps the country and nominal annual wage columns and drops rows with no wage on record.

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-height: 5
%%| fig-align: 'center'
%%| fig-caption: 'Minimum wage cleaning steps'

    sel -->|"ii. Rename"| ren["<code>country</code>, <code>annual_wage_usd</code>"]
    ren -->|"iii. Filter"| filt["Drop rows<br/>with no wage"]
    filt -->|"iv. Save"| clean[("<code>data/minimum_wage_clean.csv</code>")]
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}

## R

```{r}
#| label: clean-minimum-wage
#| message: false
#| collapse: true
library(dplyr)
library(readr)

wage_clean <- read_csv("data/minimum_wage.csv") |>
  select(matches("Country"), matches("Annual_Nominal")) |>
  rename(country = 1, annual_wage_usd = 2) |>
  mutate(annual_wage_usd = as.double(annual_wage_usd)) |>
  filter(!is.na(annual_wage_usd))
```

```{r}
#| label: view-minimum-wage
#| collapse: true
write_csv(wage_clean, "data/minimum_wage_clean.csv")
wage_clean
```

## Python

```{python}
#| label: clean-minimum-wage-py
import pandas as pd

wage = pd.read_csv("data/minimum_wage.csv")
wage_clean = wage.filter(regex="Country|Annual_Nominal").iloc[:, :2]
wage_clean.columns = ["country", "annual_wage_usd"]
wage_clean["annual_wage_usd"] = pd.to_numeric(wage_clean["annual_wage_usd"], errors="coerce")
wage_clean = wage_clean.dropna(subset=["annual_wage_usd"])
wage_clean.to_csv("data/minimum_wage_clean.csv", index=False)
wage_clean.head()
```

:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Either works

`matches()` and `filter(regex=)` both pick columns by pattern. `matches()` ignores case by default, while `filter(regex=)` doesn't, which doesn't matter for these column names.
:::

See [viz_minimum_wage.qmd](viz_minimum_wage.qmd) for the chart built on this.
